skill.name: reasoning-inductive

content.value_statement: Teams often collect observations without turning them into dependable rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured inductive reasoning with confidence bounds.
actual_capabilities: Structures multiple observations into a dataset with quality metadata.
Identifies frequency, correlation, sequence, cluster, trend, and threshold patterns.
Converts validated patterns into rules with scope, predictions, and exceptions.
Calculates confidence using sample size, pattern strength, consistency, and recency.
Defines actions, monitoring items, and data gaps from the generated rules.
limitations: Requires multiple observations before useful patterns can be formed.
Does not prove causation without separate causal validation.
Results depend on data completeness, consistency, and unbiased collection.
High-impact decisions still need expert review and domain context.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Assumptions
use_cases.description: Turn repeated customer feedback into testable rules about needs, blockers, and adoption patterns.

use_cases.title: Find Sales Process Patterns
use_cases.description: Analyze deal histories to identify recurring stalls, conversion signals, and forecast adjustments.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Research Notes
use_cases.description: Generalize findings across interviews, case studies, or field notes with stated confidence and exceptions.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a small observation set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inductive reasoning on these observations. Identify recurring patterns, weak signals, exceptions, and the confidence level for each pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Create General Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert repeated examples into practical rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these observations and form general rules. For each rule, include evidence, scope, predicted outcome, confidence bounds, and known exceptions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Suspected Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Test whether an observed trend is reliable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this suspected pattern against the observation set. Check sample size, consistency, recency, alternative explanations, and reasons to reject it.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Learning Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recurring analysis across operational records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inductive scan for these sources. Define attributes to collect, quality gates, thresholds, output sections, and review actions.

output_examples.input: Ten support tickets mention account recovery delays across two customer segments.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a recurring recovery-flow delay, separates segment-specific exceptions, and recommends collecting more timing data before automation.

output_examples.input: A sales team provides twelve recent enterprise deal notes with stage, size, duration, and outcome.
output_examples.output: The skill produces rules about legal review stalls, confidence ranges, exceptions for existing contracts, and forecast actions.

output_examples.input: A researcher has interview notes from fifteen users describing onboarding friction.
output_examples.output: The skill groups repeated onboarding issues, flags weak patterns, and states which assumptions are validated or need more evidence.

best_practices: Include both successful and failed examples to reduce selection bias.
State sample size, time range, and data quality before accepting a rule.
Record exceptions so the final rule has a clear scope.
anti_patterns: Do not form strong rules from one or two observations.
Do not treat correlation as causation without separate validation.
Do not ignore cases that challenge the preferred pattern.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps agents generalize from repeated observations into rules with evidence, confidence, and exceptions.

faq.question: How many observations are needed?
faq.answer: The skill can explore with three to five observations, but stronger rules usually need eleven or more.

faq.question: Can it prove causation?
faq.answer: No. It can identify patterns and possible mechanisms, but causal claims need separate testing.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Structured examples with consistent attributes, timestamps, outcomes, and source notes work best.

faq.question: What does the output include?
faq.answer: Outputs include detected patterns, rejected patterns, generated rules, confidence bounds, exceptions, and next actions.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
